**Headline claim (draft title):** The chat context→answer linear map does not carry over to fiction — matched transfer recovers at most 5% of ceiling, while novels host a weak, partly character-specific map (MODERATE confidence)

## Background

Parent #825 (line #779 → #825 → #810/#920) established a strong single-turn linear map from a
single-position context read (`c_last` at the assistant-header slot) to the mean answer activation
`v(x)` in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: held-out R² 0.673 at layer 19 (chat format, n=5000). This task asks
whether that map is a general character→behavior mechanism rather than an assistant/chat artifact:
(Arm A) real dialogue-rich novels (PDNC, gold speaker annotations) fed as raw text with no chat
template, predicting the mean activation over a character's attributed dialogue from that character's
intro-span context vector; (Arm B) model-written multi-character stories (fully on-policy); (Arm C)
separator-anchored spans on WikiText-103 as the persona-free genericity control. Registered reads: H1
existence (novel-held-out pooled R² @ L19 vs group-blocked shuffle band + ≥0.5× the matched-n chat
reference), H2 same-map (recentered, position-matched AND power-matched transfer fractions vs
X-recipe-matched within-regime ceilings; ≥0.5× both directions = same map, ≤0.1× either direction with
both within-maps healthy (R² > 0.2) = distinct maps), H3 specificity (ΔR²_char correct−swap with
novel-level bootstrap CI excluding 0; separator transfer < 0.5× the matched novel ceiling).

## Methodology recap (what actually ran)

- **Data:** Arm A: PDNC @ `6fda0a78`, 28 novels, 871 windows (W=3072), **1,982 pairs** (G0 gate PASS: ≥800 pairs across ≥10 novels; 0 novels dropped at the ≤10% span-mismatch gate). Arm B: 1,200 vLLM stories (T=1.0, top_p=0.95, seed 42); deterministic quote attribution kept 6,556 of 23,312 quotes (71.9% dropped, precision-first), 743 stories yielded pairs, **1,035 pairs** over 270 swap-eligible stories; Sonnet audit precision **0.914** (180/197 valid, 3 malformed judge returns dropped; binding gate 0.90 → PASS, no Batch-API re-attribution). Arm C: 600 WikiText-103 articles, **3,600 pairs**. Chat reference: reused #825 Track-S instruct turnstore (HF revision `82d3a875`, 20 files verified), n=5,000.
- **Fits:** GCV Gram ridge per layer (28 layers), K=5 GROUP folds (novel/story/article/conversation), seed 0, 20 selection-symmetric null draws, 1,000-draw group bootstrap; identical estimator to #825 (`issue825_fit_cells.heldout_r2_sweep`).
- **Gates:** G1 rig replication: layer-profile Spearman **1.000**, |ΔR² @ L19| **0.000** vs #825's committed Track-S curve — an exact reproduction because the refit is the same deterministic estimator on the same store (a code-path identity check, not an independent replication). G1b MLP-fitter parity on `chat_ref` @ L19: 0.6537 (parent `fit_h`) vs 0.6541 (batched multihead), |Δ| 0.0004 ≤ 0.02 → PASS.
- **Two R² conventions appear in the JSONs** (both reported here to avoid ambiguity): the registered headline statistic `r2_per_layer_obs` pools SS_res/SS_tot across folds with each fold's own test mean (#825 convention); the group-bootstrap block pools with the global test mean (slightly higher — e.g. Arm A within @ L19: 0.173 registered vs 0.208 bootstrap-basis, CI [0.162, 0.218]). CIs below belong to the bootstrap-basis statistic; verdicts use the registered convention on both sides of every ratio.
- **Provenance:** run executed on RunPod pod-931 (1× H100) after a GCP crash on an org-wide HF-429 quota day; on-pod canary (3 novels / 20 stories) cleared G0/G1 before production. Tensor stores + pairs metadata + stories uploaded to `superkaiba1/explore-persona-space-data / issue931_story_map/` (528 entries verified via scoped `list_repo_tree` this session).

## Results by hypothesis

### H1 (existence): a character→dialogue map exists in raw fiction — decisively above chance, but weak, and its pooled strength is mostly between-novel

| Cell (L19, registered convention) | n | groups | R² | group-CI (bootstrap basis) | max over layers | L19 null band p97.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Real-novel character map (`armA_within`) | 1,982 | 28 | **+0.173** | [0.162, 0.218] | +0.256 @ L24 | −0.086 |
| — single-position X variant (`armA_within_lastpos`) | 1,982 | 28 | +0.114 | [0.102, 0.162] | +0.189 @ L24 | −0.074 |
| Model-written story map (`armB_within`) | 1,035 | 743 | **+0.163** | [0.159, 0.174] | +0.276 @ L27 | −0.044 |
| Whole-window topic baseline (`armA_ctxmean`) | 1,982 | 28 | +0.170 | [0.157, 0.218] | +0.272 @ L24 | −0.110 |
| Chat reference (`chat_ref`) | 5,000 | 5,000 | +0.673 | [0.665, 0.682] | +0.673 @ L19 | −0.030 |

- **Shuffle-band leg: PASS, decisive.** Arm A +0.173 vs its group-blocked band (p97.5 −0.086); the selection-symmetric max-over-layers read (+0.256 @ L24) also clears its own null-max band (p97.5 −0.053). Same for Arm B. p < 0.05 by construction of the 20-draw band (0/20 null draws reach the observed value in any layer).
- **Matched-n strength leg: registered PASS at 0.547× — but fragile.** Arm A 0.173 / chat-at-n=1982 0.316 = 0.547 ≥ 0.5. The denominator sits in a **non-monotone dip of the inherited power-curve machinery**: chat R² @ L19 reads 0.495 (n=1000), 0.482 (n=1035), 0.316 (n=1982), 0.315 (n=2000), 0.673 (n=5000) — reproducing #825's committed curve exactly at shared n (0.4954 @ 1000, 0.3149 @ 2000), so the dip is inherited, not new, but a monotone interpolation (~0.5–0.55 at n≈2000) would put the fraction at ~0.31–0.35 and FAIL the 0.5× leg. I report the registered PASS with this sensitivity stated; the honest summary is "roughly one-third to one-half of chat strength at matched n."

### H3 (specificity): a character-identity component exists (CI excludes 0 in both regimes) but is small — most of the pooled signal is story/topic-level

- **Within-story character swap (registered leg 1): PASS.** ΔR²_char = R²(correct) − R²(within-story swap), both terms on the SAME derangement-eligible subset with a shared paired group-bootstrap draws matrix (the registered subset-matching concern is addressed by construction in `delta_char()`):
  - Real novels: **+0.076**, 95% novel-level CI [+0.067, +0.088] (n=1,694 pairs, 28 novels; correct-subset R² 0.209 vs swap 0.133 — the swap retains 63%).
  - Model stories: **+0.046**, CI [+0.039, +0.053] (n=562, 270 stories; 0.174 vs 0.128 — swap retains 74%; correct beats swap in 76% of stories).
- **Separator control (registered leg 2): PASS at L19 for the LINEAR map.** The separator-anchored control map has no linear signal at L19 even in-domain (own within R² −3.17; its only positive layer is L2, +0.16), and its transfer onto novel pairs is deeply negative (−95× ceiling matched; −1.20 full-n). The pre-registered topic-persistence-wins condition (separator matches novel strength AND transfers ≥0.8× AND ΔR²_char ≈ 0) fails on all three prongs.
- **But the pre-registered decomposition read fires half:** the whole-window topic baseline reaches 0.98× the character map (0.170 vs 0.173 ≥ the 0.9× trigger) while the ΔR²_char CI excludes 0 — so the registered mixed-outcome framing applies: **the pooled R² is mostly topic/story-level; character identity contributes the swap-gap only** (≈37% of the correct-subset R² in novels, ≈26% in stories).
- **The MLP secondary reframes "generic predictability":** nonlinearly, the separator control at L19 reaches R² 0.299 — larger than the character-map MLP (0.154 A / 0.142 B). Generic anchor→next-span predictability is abundant in the model nonlinearly; the H3 specificity claim is therefore scoped to the LINEAR map at L19, not to span predictability in general.
- **Unresolved confound (named, not yet measured): proximity.** By construction the correct pair's target begins immediately after C (the intro span is truncated to end right before the character's first quote), while the swapped partner's dialogue is typically farther away — so part of ΔR²_char could be local-context continuity rather than character identity. The distance-covariate read (per-pair C→T offsets from `pairs_meta`) was not computed in this round; it is the top follow-up below and is the main reason H3's specificity claim stays qualified. Related residual: no per-pair "C contains target-character speech" flag exists — the structural truncation removes the dominant leakage case, but a character's quote occurring before their first alias mention could sit inside C unflagged.
- Domain-shift note on the separator leg: the sep→novel transfer failure alone would be confounded by the WikiText→fiction corpus shift, but the control's own IN-domain L19 weakness (−3.17) shows there was no L19 linear structure to transfer in the first place; the specificity conclusion rests on the within-strength comparison + the swap, not the cross-corpus transfer.

DV = held-out activation-prediction R², the construct itself in this line (not a proxy for a judged
behavior; dual-DV N/A per plan §6). No floor/ceiling saturation: values span −3.5 to +0.67 with
dynamic range in every arm. Band-vs-ceiling: every null band's upper bound (−0.03 to −0.11 for the
character arms) sits far below the realized within-cell values, so non-rejections would have been
interpretable; all headline rejections cleared the bands regardless. Arm C's own bands are deeply
negative (p97.5 ≈ −5.8 to −6.2) and its observed cells (−3.2/−3.5) sit above them — reported as
"negative absolute R², above its pairing-permuted null," never as positive skill.

## Caveats and scope

1. Single model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), English fiction, one context-window regime (W=3072); frozen layer set inherited from #779.
2. **Matched-n denominators sit in an inherited non-monotone power-curve dip** — H1's 0.547× registered pass would fail under a monotone-interpolated denominator; H2's conclusions are robust to this (fractions ≤0.05 against either denominator).
3. **Per-novel R² is negative in 26/28 novels** — the story map is a between-novel-signal map plus a small within-window character component; do not read "R² 0.17" as within-novel predictive skill.
4. **Proximity confound on ΔR²_char unmeasured** (top follow-up); C-contains-target-speech edge case unflagged.
5. Author clustering above novels (6 Austen novels of 28) — novel-level folds and bootstrap treat them as independent; group CIs are somewhat optimistic and the between-novel component may partly be author style.
6. PDNC classics are plausibly memorized in pretraining — triangulated: the swap/shuffle contrasts are memorization-invariant, and the unmemorizable model-written Arm B reproduces every qualitative pattern (weak within-map, positive Δ, no chat transfer), so memorization does not carry the headline.
7. Arm B attribution is heuristic at audited precision 0.914 (errors attenuate Arm B toward the swap, biasing against H1/H3, not for them); 71.9% of quotes dropped precision-first.
8. Arm B's whole-window topic baseline (`armB_ctxmean`) is pathological (−0.97 @ L19) — the B1 bracket is uninformative on the story side (arm present, not missing; likely the prompt-adjacent window mean is off-distribution for story-dialogue targets).
9. G1's exact 1.000/0.000 replication is a same-code-same-data identity check, not an independent reproduction.

## Confidence

**MODERATE.** The H2 transfer failure and H1 existence are decisive, multi-arm, and pre-registered;
what keeps this off HIGH: the strength fraction's sensitivity to the power-curve dip, the unmeasured
proximity confound under ΔR²_char, single-model/English-fiction scope, and per-novel negativity making
the "map exists" claim weaker than the pooled number suggests.

### H3 (specificity): a character-identity component exists (CI excludes 0 in both regimes) but is small — most of the pooled signal is story/topic-level, and the separator leg is estimator-scoped

- **Within-story character swap (registered leg 1): PASS.** ΔR²_char = R²(correct) − R²(within-story swap), both terms on the SAME derangement-eligible subset with a shared paired group-bootstrap draws matrix (the registered subset-matching concern is addressed by construction in `delta_char()`):
  - Real novels: **+0.076**, 95% novel-level CI [+0.067, +0.088] (n=1,694 pairs, 28 novels; correct-subset R² 0.209 vs swap 0.133 — the swap retains 63%).
  - Model stories: **+0.046**, CI [+0.039, +0.053] (n=562 pairs, 270 stories; 0.174 vs 0.128 — swap retains 74%; correct beats swap in 76% of stories).
- **Separator control (registered leg 2): PASS under the registered estimator, with an estimator-dependence caveat.** Under the registered raw-basis GCV ridge, the separator control has no linear signal at L19 in-domain (within R² −3.17; positive only at the earliest layers, L0–L3 at +0.133/+0.135/+0.165/+0.136, peaking at L2), and its transfer onto novel pairs is deeply negative (−95× matched ceiling; −1.20 full-n). The pre-registered topic-persistence-wins condition (separator matches novel strength AND transfers ≥0.8× AND ΔR²_char ≈ 0) fails on all three prongs under this estimator. **However, the run's own dimension-matched random-projection control contradicts the "no linear structure" reading:** a Gaussian random-projection ridge on the SAME separator X (scrambled basis, same article-level group folds + GCV machinery) reads **+0.349** at L19 — above both character maps (0.173/0.163) and the separator MLP (0.299). The random-projection read tracks the observed fit within ±0.01 in every OTHER cell (novels 0.178 vs 0.173; stories 0.161 vs 0.163; chat 0.684 vs 0.673) and diverges by ~3.5 R² units only on the separator cell — so the −3.17 is an estimator/basis artifact (per-feature standardization + GCV shrinkage failing in the raw anchor-token basis), not absence of linear structure. Consequences: the "separator matches novel strength" prong is estimator-dependent (under a basis rotation the separator EXCEEDS the novel map); the transfer prong and the ΔR²_char prong survive; and the H3 specificity claim is scoped to the REGISTERED estimator at L19, not to linear predictability in general.
- **The pre-registered decomposition read fires half:** the whole-window topic baseline reaches 0.98× the character map (0.170 vs 0.173 ≥ the 0.9× trigger) while the ΔR²_char CI excludes 0 — so the registered mixed-outcome framing applies: **the pooled R² is mostly topic/story-level; character identity contributes the swap-gap only** (≈37% of the correct-subset R² in novels, ≈26% in stories).
- **Generic predictability is abundant at L19 in both function classes:** nonlinearly (separator MLP R² 0.299 vs character-map MLPs 0.154/0.142) AND linearly under a basis rotation (random-projection 0.349). The H3 specificity claim is therefore scoped to the registered raw-basis linear map at L19, not to span predictability in general.
- **Unresolved confound (named, not yet measured): proximity.** By construction the correct pair's target begins immediately after C (the intro span is truncated to end right before the character's first quote), while the swapped partner's dialogue is typically farther away — so part of ΔR²_char could be local-context continuity rather than character identity. The distance-covariate read (per-pair C→T offsets from `pairs_meta`) was not computed in this round; it is the top follow-up below and is the main reason H3's identity-specificity read stays LOW-to-MODERATE. Related residual: no per-pair "C contains target-character speech" flag exists — the structural truncation removes the dominant leakage case, but a character's quote occurring before their first alias mention could sit inside C unflagged.
- Domain-shift note on the separator leg: the sep→novel transfer failure alone is confounded twice — by the WikiText→fiction corpus shift AND by the registered estimator's failure on the separator cell in-domain — so the specificity conclusion rests on the within-strength comparison under the registered estimator plus the swap contrast, not on the cross-corpus transfer.

## Measurement-validity gate

DV = held-out activation-prediction R², the construct itself in this line (not a proxy for a judged
behavior; dual-DV N/A per plan §6). No floor/ceiling saturation: values span −3.5 to +0.67 with
dynamic range in every arm. Band-vs-ceiling: every null band's upper bound (−0.03 to −0.11 for the
character arms) sits far below the realized within-cell values, so non-rejections would have been
interpretable; all headline rejections cleared the bands regardless. Arm C's own bands are deeply
negative (p97.5 ≈ −5.8 to −6.2) and its observed cells (−3.2/−3.5) sit above them — reported as
"negative absolute R², above its pairing-permuted null," never as positive skill; the random-projection
read (+0.349) is the estimator-robust statement of Arm C's in-domain linear predictability.

## Caveats and scope

1. Single model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), English fiction, one context-window regime (W=3072); frozen layer set inherited from #779.
2. **Matched-n denominators sit in an inherited non-monotone power-curve dip and are single-seed** — H1's 0.547× registered pass would fail under a monotone-interpolated denominator; the chat→novel matched-transfer NUMERATOR inherits the same regime; H2's conclusions are robust to this (chat-side fractions ≤0.05 against either denominator).
3. **Per-novel R² is negative in 26/28 novels** — the story map is a between-novel-signal map plus a small within-window character component; do not read "R² 0.17" as within-novel predictive skill.
4. **Proximity confound on ΔR²_char unmeasured** (top follow-up); C-contains-target-speech edge case unflagged. H3 identity-specificity is LOW-to-MODERATE for this reason.
5. Author clustering above novels (6 Austen novels of 28) — novel-level folds and bootstrap treat them as independent; group CIs are somewhat optimistic and the between-novel component may partly be author style. Concretely: the only two positive per-novel cells (Mansfield Park +0.026, Sense and Sensibility +0.017) are Austen, Pride and Prejudice sits at ≈0 (−0.001), and 6 of the top 7 per-novel ranks are Austen/Forster.
6. PDNC classics are plausibly memorized in pretraining — triangulated: the swap/shuffle contrasts are memorization-invariant, and the unmemorizable model-written Arm B reproduces every qualitative pattern (weak within-map, positive Δ, no chat transfer), so memorization does not carry the headline.
7. Arm B attribution is heuristic at audited precision 0.914 (errors attenuate Arm B toward the swap, biasing against H1/H3, not for them); 71.9% of quotes dropped precision-first.
8. Arm B's whole-window topic baseline (`armB_ctxmean`) is pathological (−0.97 @ L19) — the B1 bracket is uninformative on the story side (arm present, not missing; likely the prompt-adjacent window mean is off-distribution for story-dialogue targets).
9. G1's exact 1.000/0.000 replication is a same-code-same-data identity check, not an independent reproduction.
10. **The registered raw-basis ridge estimator fails specifically on the separator cell** (random-projection control +0.349 vs raw-basis −3.17 at L19, while agreeing within ±0.01 everywhere else) — every "separator has no linear signal"-flavored statement is scoped to the registered estimator, and the H3 leg-2 strength prong is estimator-dependent.

## Confidence

**MODERATE overall.** The H2 transfer failure (now control-referenced on the positive side too) and H1
existence are decisive, multi-arm, and pre-registered. **H3 identity-specificity is LOW-to-MODERATE**:
the swap-gap CIs exclude 0 in both regimes, but the proximity confound is unmeasured and all matched-n
denominators are single-seed. What keeps the whole off HIGH: the strength fraction's sensitivity to the
power-curve dip, the unmeasured proximity confound, the separator-cell estimator artifact, single-model
/ English-fiction scope, and per-novel negativity making the "map exists" claim weaker than the pooled
number suggests.

1. **Chat→fiction transfer fails decisively, and the one positive chat-side read is small and not distinctive.** Recentered power-matched fractions at L19 span −97 to +0.05 of ceiling across all chat-side directions; the best positive, novel→chat at +0.048 of matched ceiling (transfer R² +0.015), is a level a persona-free WikiText separator map also reaches when fit on its full n=3,600 source (+0.073 = +0.231 of the same n=1982 ceiling; an unmatched reference — 1.8× more source data), while the SOURCE-MATCHED control computed this round (the separator map refit on a seeded n=1,982 subsample) collapses to −4.05 with its source fit inside the registered estimator's known failure regime on WikiText anchor-token inputs — so the control family brackets the positive read without adjudicating its genericity, and the read stays an order of magnitude below the registered 0.5× same-map bar either way.
2. **A character→dialogue map exists in raw fiction but is weak and mostly between-novel/topic.** Pooled held-out R² +0.173 (real novels, n=1,982 pairs / 28 novels) and +0.163 (model stories, n=1,035 / 743) clear group-blocked shuffle bands decisively (p97.5 −0.086 / −0.044), yet per-novel R² is negative in 26 of 28 novels and a whole-window topic baseline reaches 0.98× the map (0.170 vs 0.173).

## Background

Parent #825 (line #779 → #825 → #810/#920) established a strong single-turn linear map from a
single-position context read (`c_last` at the assistant-header slot) to the mean answer activation
`v(x)` in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: held-out R² 0.673 at layer 19 (chat format, n=5000). This task asks
whether that map is a general character→behavior mechanism rather than an assistant/chat artifact:
(Arm A) real dialogue-rich novels (PDNC, gold speaker annotations) fed as raw text with no chat
template, predicting the mean activation over a character's attributed dialogue from that character's
intro-span context vector; (Arm B) model-written multi-character stories (fully on-policy); (Arm C)
separator-anchored spans on WikiText-103 as the persona-free genericity control. Registered reads: H1
existence (novel-held-out pooled R² @ L19 vs group-blocked shuffle band + ≥0.5× the matched-n chat
reference), H2 same-map (recentered, position-matched AND power-matched transfer fractions vs
X-recipe-matched within-regime ceilings; ≥0.5× both directions = same map, ≤0.1× either direction with
both within-maps healthy (R² > 0.2) = distinct maps), H3 specificity (ΔR²_char correct−swap with
novel-level bootstrap CI excluding 0; separator transfer < 0.5× the matched novel ceiling).

## Methodology recap (what actually ran)

- **Data:** Arm A: PDNC @ `6fda0a78`, 28 novels, 871 windows (W=3072), **1,982 pairs** (G0 gate PASS: ≥800 pairs across ≥10 novels; 0 novels dropped at the ≤10% span-mismatch gate). Arm B: 1,200 vLLM stories (T=1.0, top_p=0.95, seed 42); deterministic quote attribution kept 6,556 of 23,312 quotes (71.9% dropped, precision-first); **1,035 pairs across 743 stories**; the within-story swap subset is **562 pairs over the 270 swap-eligible stories** (stories contributing ≥2 characters); Sonnet audit precision **0.914** (180/197 valid, 3 malformed judge returns dropped; binding gate 0.90 → PASS, no Batch-API re-attribution). Arm C: 600 WikiText-103 articles, **3,600 pairs**. Chat reference: reused #825 Track-S instruct turnstore (HF revision `82d3a875`, 20 files verified), n=5,000.
- **Fits:** GCV Gram ridge per layer (28 layers), K=5 GROUP folds (novel/story/article/conversation), seed 0, 20 selection-symmetric null draws, 1,000-draw group bootstrap; identical estimator to #825 (`issue825_fit_cells.heldout_r2_sweep`).
- **Gates:** G1 rig replication: layer-profile Spearman **1.000**, |ΔR² @ L19| **0.000** vs #825's committed Track-S curve — an exact reproduction because the refit is the same deterministic estimator on the same store (a code-path identity check, not an independent replication). G1b MLP-fitter parity on the chat reference @ L19: 0.6537 (parent `fit_h`) vs 0.6541 (batched multihead), |Δ| 0.0004 ≤ 0.02 → PASS.
- **Two R² conventions appear in the JSONs** (both reported here to avoid ambiguity): the registered headline statistic `r2_per_layer_obs` pools SS_res/SS_tot across folds with each fold's own test mean (#825 convention); the group-bootstrap block pools with the global test mean (slightly higher — e.g. Arm A within @ L19: 0.173 registered vs 0.208 bootstrap-basis, CI [0.162, 0.218]). CIs below belong to the bootstrap-basis statistic; verdicts use the registered convention on both sides of every ratio.
- **Round-2 control:** separator→chat transfer computed from the run's SAVED fp16 full-n (3,600) maps (`issue931_story_map/analysis_tensors/maps/armC_sep_L19.pt`) applied to the pinned #825 chat store via the run's own `transfer_r2` (recentered, 5 group folds, seed 0, 20 pairing-null draws). | — single-position X variant (`armA_within_lastpos`) | 1,982 | 28 | +0.114 | [0.102, 0.162] | +0.189 @ L24 | −0.074 |
| Model-written story map (`armB_within`) | 1,035 | 743 | **+0.163** | [0.159, 0.174] | +0.276 @ L27 | −0.044 |
| Whole-window topic baseline (`armA_ctxmean`) | 1,982 | 28 | +0.170 | [0.157, 0.218] | +0.272 @ L24 | −0.110 |
| Chat reference (`chat_ref`) | 5,000 | 5,000 | +0.673 | [0.665, 0.682] | +0.673 @ L19 | −0.030 |

- **Shuffle-band leg: PASS, decisive.** Arm A +0.173 vs its group-blocked band (p97.5 −0.086); the selection-symmetric max-over-layers read (+0.256 @ L24) also clears its own null-max band (p97.5 −0.053). Same for Arm B. p < 0.05 by construction of the 20-draw band (0/20 null draws reach the observed value in any layer).
- **Matched-n strength leg: registered PASS at 0.547× — but fragile.** Arm A 0.173 / chat-at-n=1982 0.316 = 0.547 ≥ 0.5. The denominator sits in a **non-monotone dip of the inherited power-curve machinery**: chat R² @ L19 reads 0.495 (n=1000), 0.482 (n=1035), 0.316 (n=1982), 0.315 (n=2000), 0.673 (n=5000) — reproducing #825's committed curve exactly at shared n (0.4954 @ 1000, 0.3149 @ 2000), so the dip is inherited, not new, but a monotone interpolation (~0.5–0.55 at n≈2000) would put the fraction at ~0.31–0.35 and FAIL the 0.5× leg. I report the registered PASS with this sensitivity stated; the honest summary is "roughly one-third to one-half of chat strength at matched n."
- **The pooled R² is carried by between-novel variation.** Per-novel R² (each novel's own variance as denominator) is negative in **26 of 28 novels** (only Mansfield Park +0.026 and Sense and Sensibility +0.017 positive; Alice in Wonderland −1.30 is the extreme outlier). Within a novel, the map's predictions are worse than that novel's own mean target — the pooled positive R² reflects predicting which-novel/which-window-level differences. The character-level content is only visible in the paired swap contrast (H3). Same pattern in Arm B: per-story R² is negative for all 270 swap-eligible stories under the correct pairing too (the remaining 473 stories contribute one pair each, so their per-story R² is undefined and excluded — "all 270" is out of the 270 with a defined value, not 270 of 743); the paired contrast still favors correct in 76% of stories.
- **The intro-span recipe adds ~nothing over a character-agnostic whole-window mean at the pooled level** (0.173 vs 0.170), and the parent-matched single-position X is weaker than the span mean in both regimes (A: 0.114 vs 0.173; B: 0.080 vs 0.163). The MLP secondary does not rescue the linear map (Arm A MLP 0.154 @ L19 vs ridge 0.173) — unlike #825's two-turn case, there is no hidden nonlinear character map here.
- **Layer profiles differ from chat:** the story maps peak late (L24/L27) where chat peaks at L19; profile Spearman vs chat is 0.703 (A) / 0.776 (B) — at the 0.7 convergent-read threshold (but see H2: profile similarity is not diagnostic).

- **The "same map" leg (≥0.5× both directions) is missed by an order of magnitude,** and the best chat-side fraction — novel→chat at +0.048 (transfer +0.015, above its pairing-permuted null p97.5 −0.016) — is BRACKETED by the two persona-free control reads rather than cleanly adjudicated. The round-2 FULL-n control (separator map at its full n=3,600 source — a 1.8× data advantage over the novel source) transfers at +0.073 = +0.231 of the same ceiling, showing a persona-free anchor→next-span map CAN produce a chat-side transfer of this size; because of its data advantage it is an unmatched upper reference, informative only in the detect-sharing direction (novel→chat exceeding it would have been evidence of sharing; it does not). The round-3 SOURCE-MATCHED control (n=1,982 seeded subsample refit — the run's own matched-power machinery) collapses to −4.05 (above its own pairing null p97.5 −4.41, the generic above-null pattern, but deeply negative — an output-scale mismatch in the same family as the chat→novel −11.11 read), so at equal budget the persona-free map does NOT out-transfer the novel map. The matched control's source fit, however, sits exactly in the raw-basis estimator-failure regime the run's random-projection control exposes on WikiText inputs (the separator cell's own within-R² is −0.50 matched / −3.17 full-n under the registered estimator), so its collapse is plausibly estimator pathology at reduced n rather than a clean genericity read. Net: the persona-free-control comparison neither establishes nor rules out generic anchor→next-span structure behind the +0.048; the same-map verdict rests on the fraction being 10× below the registered 0.5× bar, not on the control. (Story-gen→chat +0.039 is bracketed identically.)
- **The catastrophic chat→novel magnitude is a scale artifact at the pairing-null floor, amplified by the dip regime.** The matched −11.11 sits AT its own permuted-pairing null (p97.5 −10.96) — the entire magnitude is what the same frozen subsampled map produces on permuted pairings (output-scale mismatch), carrying ≈ zero pairing information. The matched NUMERATOR (the n*=1982 chat source fit) also inherits the same anomalous n≈2000 chat-fit regime as the H1 denominator: the full-n chat→novel transfer is −0.70, 16× less negative. The regime-robust part of the H2 verdict is the ≤0.05 positive chat-side fractions, which hold under both matched and full-n denominators. The strict-frozen secondary is worse still (−15.6), so recentering absorbs part but not most of the failure. Note that at full n even the NEGATIVE transfers clear their pairing-permuted nulls — chat→novel −0.70 vs p97.5 −0.82, chat→story −0.40 vs −0.53, separator→novel −0.14 vs −0.23 — i.e. "above the pairing null" is generic (the persona-free control shows it too) and is not evidence of chat↔fiction sharing; this is exactly why every positive read here is referenced against the control rather than its null.
- **The registered "distinct maps" leg does not formally fire either**: it requires both within-maps healthy (R² > 0.2 at matched budget), and the novel within-map is itself weak (single-position X 0.114; span-mean 0.173). The result lands in a corner the lattice did not register: transfers ≤ 0.1× ceiling with a weak story-side map. Per the plan, the graded weight-level reads then govern:
  - **Output (left) subspace overlap chat↔novel @ L19 is modestly above the random-subspace null but below the separator-control reference** — 0.007/0.022/0.083 at k=16/64/256 vs null p97.5 0.005/0.018/0.072 (1.2–1.4×), against the separator-control reference 0.011/0.031/0.107. Above-null overlap is thus generic; under the control-as-reference standard it reads as residual-stream anisotropy, not shared mechanism.
  - **Input (right) overlap is above the null (0.23–0.30) but does NOT exceed the control reference** — the separator-control map's overlap with the novel map is higher (0.28–0.34); same conclusion.
  - **Prediction CKA @ L19:** chat↔novel 0.227 — above the separator↔novel control (0.197) but far below the preceding-sentence↔novel control (0.624); anchored on the preceding-sentence reference, CKA similarity at this level is not diagnostic of sharing.
  - **Layer-profile Spearman** chat↔novel 0.703 sits exactly at the 0.7 convergent threshold — but the preceding-sentence control reaches 0.852 vs chat, so profile similarity is also not diagnostic. The preceding-sentence control makes the point sharply: under the registered raw-basis estimator it has deeply negative predictive R² at EVERY layer (max −3.40 @ L27, −3.50 @ L19) yet shows the highest profile-Spearman vs chat (0.852) and the highest CKA vs the novel map (0.624). Its rotated-basis read (+0.334, random-projection control) shows it DOES carry generic linear anchor→span structure — which strengthens the conclusion rather than weakening it: profile/CKA similarity reads track generic linear structure these activation geometries share, not a working shared character map.
- **The two fiction regimes share a little with each other:** novel→story-gen +0.147/+0.213 of ceiling, left-subspace overlap 0.025/0.054/0.159 (2.2–4.7× the random null and modestly above the preceding-sentence control 0.012/0.040/0.126) — weak partial sharing between the two character maps, asymmetric (story-gen→novel is negative).
- The novel→separator row renders "n/a" in the transfer figure because its FRACTION is undefined, not because the transfer failed to compute: the transfer R² is +0.019 (above its pairing null p97.5 −0.012), but the separator cell's own within-ceiling is negative under the registered estimator (−0.50 matched subsample / −3.17 full-n), so fraction-of-ceiling is meaningless there.

Bottom line for H2: **no evidence of one shared context→behavior map across chat and fiction.** The
defensible claim is directional — the chat map's linear structure does not apply to fiction character
pairs (chat-side fractions ≤0.05 vs the registered 0.5× bar, with catastrophic reverse directions);
every weight-level similarity read (left/right overlaps, CKA, layer profiles) sits at or below its
persona-free reference; and the one positive transfer read is small and bracketed inconclusively by
the control family (full-n control above it, estimator-compromised matched control far below) — while
noting the story-side map's weakness means a small shared component below the detection level cannot
be excluded ("failure to detect sharing," not "proof of disjoint mechanisms").

### H3 (specificity): a character-identity component exists (CI excludes 0 in both regimes) but is small — most of the pooled signal is story/topic-level, and the separator leg is estimator-scoped

- **Within-story character swap (registered leg 1): PASS.** ΔR²_char = R²(correct) − R²(within-story swap), both terms on the SAME derangement-eligible subset with a shared paired group-bootstrap draws matrix (the registered subset-matching concern is addressed by construction in `delta_char()`):
  - Real novels: **+0.076**, 95% novel-level CI [+0.067, +0.088] (n=1,694 pairs, 28 novels; correct-subset R² 0.209 vs swap 0.133 — the swap retains 63%).
  - Model stories: **+0.046**, CI [+0.039, +0.053] (n=562 pairs, 270 stories; 0.174 vs 0.128 — swap retains 74%; correct beats swap in 76% of stories).
- **Separator control (registered leg 2): PASS under the registered estimator, with an estimator-dependence caveat that covers BOTH WikiText control cells.** Under the registered raw-basis GCV ridge, the separator control has no linear signal at L19 in-domain (within R² −3.17; positive only at the earliest layers, L0–L3 at +0.133/+0.135/+0.165/+0.136, peaking at L2), and its transfer onto novel pairs is deeply negative (−95× matched ceiling; −1.20 full-n). The pre-registered topic-persistence-wins condition (separator matches novel strength AND transfers ≥0.8× AND ΔR²_char ≈ 0) fails on all three prongs under this estimator. **However, the run's own dimension-matched random-projection control contradicts the "no linear structure" reading on both Arm-C cells:** a Gaussian random-projection ridge on the SAME X (scrambled basis, same article-level group folds + GCV machinery) reads **+0.349** on the separator cell and **+0.334** on the preceding-sentence cell at L19 — above both character maps (0.173/0.163) and comparable to the separator MLP (0.299) — where the raw basis reads −3.17 / −3.50. The raw-basis estimator thus fails on exactly the two cells built from the WikiText anchor-token X recipe, tracks the observed fit within ±0.011 on the eight cells with healthy raw fits (novels 0.178 vs 0.173; stories 0.161 vs 0.163; chat 0.684 vs 0.673; the swap/topic/single-position variants likewise), and disagrees by ~0.67 in the OPPOSITE direction on the already-flagged pathological model-story topic baseline (rotation −1.64 vs raw −0.97). The failure being confined to one shared X recipe makes the estimator/basis-artifact diagnosis MORE coherent, not less — per-feature standardization + GCV shrinkage failing in the raw anchor-token basis, not absence of linear structure. Consequences: the "separator matches novel strength" prong is estimator-dependent (under a basis rotation BOTH WikiText controls EXCEED the character maps); the transfer prong and the ΔR²_char prong survive; and the specificity claim is scoped to the REGISTERED estimator at L19, not to linear predictability in general.
- **The pre-registered decomposition read fires half:** the whole-window topic baseline reaches 0.98× the character map (0.170 vs 0.173 ≥ the 0.9× trigger) while the ΔR²_char CI excludes 0 — so the registered mixed-outcome framing applies: **the pooled R² is mostly topic/story-level; character identity contributes the swap-gap only** (≈37% of the correct-subset R² in novels, ≈26% in stories).
- **Generic predictability is abundant at L19 in both function classes:** nonlinearly (separator MLP R² 0.299 vs character-map MLPs 0.154/0.142) AND linearly under a basis rotation (random-projection +0.349 separator / +0.334 preceding-sentence). The specificity claim is therefore scoped to the registered raw-basis linear map at L19, not to span predictability in general.
- **Unresolved confound (named, not yet measured): proximity.** By construction the correct pair's target begins immediately after C (the intro span is truncated to end right before the character's first quote), while the swapped partner's dialogue is typically farther away — so part of ΔR²_char could be local-context continuity rather than character identity. The distance-covariate read (per-pair C→T offsets from `pairs_meta`) was not computed in this round; it is the top follow-up below and is the main reason the identity-specificity read stays LOW-to-MODERATE (see Confidence). Related residual: no per-pair "C contains target-character speech" flag exists — the structural truncation removes the dominant leakage case, but a character's quote occurring before their first alias mention could sit inside C unflagged.
- Domain-shift note on the separator leg: the sep→novel transfer failure alone is confounded twice — by the WikiText→fiction corpus shift AND by the registered estimator's failure on the separator cell in-domain — so the specificity conclusion rests on the within-strength comparison under the registered estimator plus the swap contrast, not on the cross-corpus transfer.

## Measurement-validity gate

DV = held-out activation-prediction R², the construct itself in this line (not a proxy for a judged
behavior; dual-DV N/A per plan §6). No floor/ceiling saturation: values span −3.5 to +0.67 with
dynamic range in every arm. Band-vs-ceiling: every null band's upper bound (−0.03 to −0.11 for the
character arms) sits far below the realized within-cell values, so non-rejections would have been
interpretable; all headline rejections cleared the bands regardless. Arm C's own bands are deeply
negative (p97.5 ≈ −5.8 to −6.2) and its observed cells (−3.2/−3.5) sit above them — reported as
"negative absolute R², above its pairing-permuted null," never as positive skill; the random-projection
reads (+0.349 separator, +0.334 preceding-sentence) are the estimator-robust statement of Arm C's
in-domain linear predictability.

## Caveats and scope

1. Single model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), English fiction, one context-window regime (W=3072); frozen layer set inherited from #779.
2. **Matched-n denominators sit in an inherited non-monotone power-curve dip and are single-seed** — the registered 0.547× existence pass would fail under a monotone-interpolated denominator; the chat→novel matched-transfer NUMERATOR inherits the same regime; the transfer conclusions are robust to this (chat-side fractions ≤0.05 against either denominator).
3. **Per-novel R² is negative in 26/28 novels** — the story map is a between-novel-signal map plus a small within-window character component; do not read "R² 0.17" as within-novel predictive skill.
4. **Proximity confound on ΔR²_char unmeasured** (top follow-up); C-contains-target-speech edge case unflagged. The identity-specificity read is LOW-to-MODERATE for this reason (see Confidence).
5. Author clustering above novels (6 Austen novels of 28) — novel-level folds and bootstrap treat them as independent; group CIs are somewhat optimistic and the between-novel component may partly be author style. Concretely: the only two positive per-novel cells (Mansfield Park +0.026, Sense and Sensibility +0.017) are Austen, Pride and Prejudice sits at ≈0 (−0.001), and 6 of the top 7 per-novel ranks are Austen/Forster.
6. PDNC classics are plausibly memorized in pretraining — triangulated: the swap/shuffle contrasts are memorization-invariant, and the unmemorizable model-written Arm B reproduces every qualitative pattern (weak within-map, positive Δ, no chat transfer), so memorization does not carry the headline.
7. Arm B attribution is heuristic at audited precision 0.914 (errors attenuate Arm B toward the swap, biasing against the existence and specificity reads, not for them); 71.9% of quotes dropped precision-first.
8. Arm B's whole-window topic baseline (`armB_ctxmean`) is pathological (−0.97 @ L19; the random-projection rotation reads it MORE negative, −1.64) — the B1 bracket is uninformative on the story side (arm present, not missing; likely the prompt-adjacent window mean is off-distribution for story-dialogue targets).
9. G1's exact 1.000/0.000 replication is a same-code-same-data identity check, not an independent reproduction.
